record.category: ad-monetised video host (pay-per-view) with free storage, HLS streaming

free_tier.stated: "Earn Money & Share Videos - Your videos are stored the safest fastest and earn real money." The meta description states the offer plainly: "Storage is completely Free."
free_tier.notes: The page never prints a number for storage, bandwidth or earnings; the word is 'Free' with no qualifier.

egress.terms: "no speed caps on data transfer rates" and HLS distribution across multiple cloud servers 'for redundancy and security'. No allowance or price is printed.

record.interface_detail: Web upload and an embed player. The page read documents no API, FTP or remote upload, unlike LuluStream in the same class.
record.tooling: Browser only as read. For a user that needs programmatic ingest this is the weaker of the two video hosts recorded among debrid providers, and the gap is a tooling note rather than a verdict.
record.chaining: A free place to park long-tail video that is served through an embed. Less useful than LuluStream here because ingest is manual, and useful at all only for content that does not change often.
record.limits_note: Nothing measurable is published. The page is a publisher pitch with an earnings programme, not a specification.
record.binding_note: No published counter exists to name. As with every free video host here, what ends an account is enforcement (bandwidth that does not earn, or a complaint), not a quota that can be planned against.

identity_cost.detail: Registration is required to publish ('Get start now' leads to ?op=registration) and payouts imply a payment identity; the form itself was not read.

record.reliability_note: The page still calls itself 'EarnVids' in its own feature descriptions while the domain and title say VidHide, which is a rebrand not finished in the copy. That is a small signal that the operation changes names, and a client's links die with the name.
record.confidence_note: Read on the live site. Thin by the vendor's design: three claims, no numbers. The record's value is the classification and the rebrand signal, not a capacity figure.

evidence.proved: 'Storage is completely Free' in the meta description, 'no speed caps on data transfer rates', HLS distribution, and the leftover 'EarnVids' naming in the feature copy

record.notes: Kept as its own record because the name appears in host lists and a session will otherwise re-open it; the capacity claim is not repeated as fact.
